reason: The text depicts and reinforces strict hierarchy rather than discouraging it. It establishes clear authority structures: the priest/father (Reuel) maintains absolute authority over his daughters; the daughters are subordinate and dependent, required to serve their father's needs (watering his flocks) and report to him; gender hierarchy is evident as the daughters require male assistance (Moses) when confronted by shepherds; and patriarchal authority is normalized when the father unilaterally decides to give his daughter (Zipporah) in marriage to Moses. The narrative presents these hierarchical relationships as the proper social order without any indication of criticism or challenge to this structure.
